title: Month 24
subtitle: Two years. The two-year visit is this month, and it is the second autism screen.

baby.development: Your child says fifty or more words, puts two together, and can run, kick, and climb. They can follow a two-step instruction and are starting to sort by shape and color.

you.body: Two years of carrying a child is two years of a body doing more than it did before. If something hurts, it is worth a physio visit.
you.mind: Two is a real milestone and it is worth noticing. The next year is the year of sentences, and it is easier than the year of tantrums.

coreActions.title: Go to the two-year visit
coreActions.why: This is the second autism screen, the language check, and the visit where the next year's schedule gets set.
coreActions.detail: The two-year visit usually has no vaccines if the eighteen-month set is complete. The doctor will do a second autism screen and check language, movement, teeth, and growth. Ask about the next visit, which is at thirty months.

coreActions.title: Model three words together
coreActions.why: Three-word sentences usually arrive between twenty-four and thirty months, and they come from hearing them.
coreActions.detail: When the child says two words, give three back: more milk becomes more milk please. Ask questions that need more than yes or no. Narrate what you are doing. Do not correct, expand.

coreActions.title: Put a potty in the bathroom, and do not push it
coreActions.why: A potty that is just there, with no pressure, is what makes the later attempt quick.
coreActions.detail: Put a potty in the bathroom the child uses. Let them sit on it clothed if they want. Talk about what the toilet is for. Do not start training until the child shows the readiness signs, which for most is between two and three.

personas.headline: You are the other half of the discipline
personas.body: A two-year-old learns what is allowed by testing both of you. Two different answers is a lesson in which parent to ask.

actions.title: Agree on the one rule
actions.why: Pick the thing you will both hold, and hold it the same way. One rule held is worth ten announced.

actions.title: Take them out on your own
actions.why: An hour at the park, without her, is an hour she is not being climbed on.

personas.headline: You are the safe place with the boring rules
personas.body: A toddler who knows your house has the same rules as their house is a toddler who can relax. That is the gift.

actions.title: Match their rules at your house
actions.why: If the cot has no blanket at home, it has no blanket at yours. Consistency is what makes you restful.

actions.title: Back the parent up in front of the child
actions.why: Disagree later, in the kitchen. A toddler who sees you overrule a parent learns to shop for the softer answer.

personas.headline: This is when you become the fun one
personas.body: A two-year-old cannot be charmed, but can be delighted. You are the person with no rules to enforce and no bedtime to defend.

actions.title: Take them somewhere with weather
actions.why: Puddles, sticks, a hill. The outing that costs nothing is the one they talk about.

actions.title: Ask the parent first
actions.why: A sweet before dinner is not your call. Ask once, in front of the child, and take the answer.

alsoKnow.title: Milk comes down to about sixteen ounces
alsoKnow.body: After two, whole milk is no longer needed and 2% is fine. Keep it to about sixteen ounces a day, in a cup, with meals.

alsoKnow.title: Two is when the screen rules get tested
alsoKnow.body: The recommendation for two to five is no more than an hour a day of high-quality content, watched with an adult. A child who has had no screens until two will ask for them now, because they see them everywhere.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
A fall from furniture, or a head injury with vomiting or unusual sleepiness
